title: Restore IP Addresses
summary: Given a string s consisting solely of digits, generate all possible valid IP addresses by inserting dots.
statement: Given a string s consisting solely of digits, generate all possible valid IP addresses by inserting dots. Each segment of the resulting IP address must be an integer between 0 and 255, inclusive, with no leading zeros. Return the valid IP addresses in any order, ensuring no digits are reordered or removed from s.
constraints: 1–20 decimal digits. Insert exactly three dots without deleting or reordering digits.
Every segment must be 0–255 with no leading zero except the single digit 0. Return all distinct valid addresses in any order.
hints: A valid address uses four segments, each one to three digits long.
Choose the next segment length, validate it, then recurse on the remaining digits.
Reject if remaining digit count cannot fit the remaining slots; accept only after four segments consume the entire string.
Check both the numerical upper bound and the no-leading-zero rule before descending.
editorial: Backtrack over segment lengths one, two, and three. Reject leading-zero segments longer than one digit and values above 255. Track how many of the four segments remain and prune when the remaining digits cannot fill them. A completed choice is accepted only after consuming every digit. There are at most 3^4 length-choice branches; forming output strings adds a bounded factor of the input length. The oracle enumerates triples of cut positions instead.

tests.explanation: Only 0.0.0.0 is valid; longer segments such as 00 have forbidden leading zeros.
